explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. `Place`, `Divisor`, `Divisor.degree` and `Divisor.degZero` (the kernel of `degree`) are all the library's own definitions, from Definitions/Def_AlgebraicCurve_DivisorClassGroup.lean, and Mathlib has nothing comparable for places of function fields. The theorem says that if every place has degree 1, then the divisor of P minus the divisor of Q has degree 0. The proof only rewrites with the library's own lemmas `Divisor.mem_degZero` and `Divisor.degree_single`, plus the generic `map_sub` and `sub_self`. So the content comes from the library's definitions, not from a Mathlib result. I only grepped the library to confirm where these definitions come from; I did not run a separate name or content search in Mathlib, since it has no function-field places or divisors of this kind to match.
